{{Short description|Probability problem}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Stieltjes [[moment problem]]''', named after [[Thomas Joannes Stieltjes]], seeks necessary and sufficient conditions for a [[sequence]] (''m''<sub>0</sub>, ''m''<sub>1</sub>, ''m''<sub>2</sub>, ...) to be of the form

:<math>m_n = \int_0^\infty x^n\,d\mu(x)</math>

for some [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] ''&mu;''. If such a function ''&mu;'' exists, one asks whether it is unique.

The essential difference between this and other well-known [[moment problem]]s is that this is on a half-line <nowiki>[</nowiki>0,&nbsp;&infin;<nowiki>)</nowiki>, whereas in the [[Hausdorff moment problem]] one considers a [[Interval (mathematics)#Definitions|bounded interval]] [0,&nbsp;1], and in the [[Hamburger moment problem]] one considers the whole line (−&infin;,&nbsp;&infin;).

==Existence==
Let

:<math>\Delta_n=\left[\begin{matrix}
m_0 & m_1 & m_2 & \cdots & m_{n}    \\
m_1 & m_2 & m_3 & \cdots & m_{n+1} \\
m_2& m_3 & m_4 & \cdots & m_{n+2} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
m_{n} & m_{n+1} & m_{n+2} & \cdots & m_{2n}
\end{matrix}\right]</math>

be a [[Hankel matrix]], and

:<math>\Delta_n^{(1)}=\left[\begin{matrix}
m_1 & m_2 & m_3 & \cdots & m_{n+1}    \\
m_2 & m_3 & m_4 & \cdots & m_{n+2} \\
m_3 & m_4 & m_5 & \cdots & m_{n+3} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
m_{n+1} & m_{n+2} & m_{n+3} & \cdots & m_{2n+1}
\end{matrix}\right].</math>

Then {&nbsp;''m''<sub>''n''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;3,&nbsp;...&nbsp;} is a moment sequence of some measure on <math>[0,\infty)</math> with infinite support if and only if for all ''n'', both

:<math>\det(\Delta_n) > 0\ \mathrm{and}\ \det\left(\Delta_n^{(1)}\right) > 0.</math>

{&nbsp;''m''<sub>''n''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;3,&nbsp;...&nbsp;} is a moment sequence of some measure on <math>[0,\infty)</math> with finite support of size ''m'' if and only if for all <math>n \leq m</math>, both

:<math>\det(\Delta_n) > 0\ \mathrm{and}\ \det\left(\Delta_n^{(1)}\right) > 0</math>

and for all larger <math>n</math>

:<math>\det(\Delta_n) = 0\ \mathrm{and}\ \det\left(\Delta_n^{(1)}\right) = 0.</math>

==Uniqueness==

There are several sufficient conditions for uniqueness.

'''[[Carleman's condition]]''': The solution is unique if

:<math> \sum_{n \geq 1} m_n^{-1/(2n)} = \infty~.</math>
'''[[G. H. Hardy|Hardy]]'s criterion''': If <math>\mu</math> is a [[probability distribution]] supported on <math>[0, \infty)</math>, such that <math>\mathbb E_{X \sim \mu}[e^{c\sqrt{X}}] < \infty</math>, then all its moments are finite, and <math>\mu</math> is the unique distribution with these moments.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stoyanov |first=J. |last2=Lin |first2=G. D. |date=January 2013 |title=Hardy's Condition in the Moment Problem for Probability Distributions |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S0040585X9798631X |journal=Theory of Probability & Its Applications |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=699–708 |doi=10.1137/S0040585X9798631X |issn=0040-585X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Hardy |first=G. H. |date=1917 |title=On Stieltjes' "problème des moments" |journal=Messenger of Mathematics |volume=46 |pages=175–182}}. Reprinted in {{cite book |author=Hardy, G. H. |title=Collected Papers of G. H. Hardy |date=1979 |publisher=Oxford University Press |volume=VII |location=Oxford |pages=75–83}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Hardy |first=G. H. |date=1918 |title=On Stieltjes' "problème des moments" (continued) |journal=Messenger of Mathematics |volume=47 |pages=81–88}}. Reprinted in {{cite book |author=Hardy, G. H. |title=Collected Papers of G. H. Hardy |date=1979 |publisher=Oxford University Press |volume=VII |location=Oxford |pages=84–91}}</ref>
